brief: Goldman's Pasquariello calls Q3 "tricky": Magnificent Seven +11%, cap-weighted S&P +2%, equal-weight S&P -2%, Russell -8%, while the 10-year yield rose 82bps. Leaders led on earnings growth, laggards lagged on rates and oil. The momentum factor swung -30% in July, -14% in August, +27% in September, making the trend harder to ride than it looked. META rose 25% in a month on agentic-AI demand, MU rallied on earnings despite a high multiple, and NVDA added $150bn to its buyback, now $235bn total. NDX rallied 11 of 13 days despite rising rates because September capital flows concentrated in these names. Investors stay underweight Asia despite sell-side targets implying ~90% upside. TOPIX rose 20.0% YTD locally and the Nikkei 36.6% versus ~11.8% for the S&P, though JPY swings keep it from feeling like a winning tape. Europe lags given its sovereign-debt stack. Persian Gulf oil exports are back to 2025's average despite Iran tensions. Pasquariello likes the Q4 setup: quarter-end supply is done, funds have shed length, buybacks resume, and retail sat out September. The rally is narrow: whether mega-cap tech stays "duration resistant" decides if 7700 is a pause before higher highs, since Europe, Asia, and oil offer no second engine.
